correctness.rationale: With a fixed proper vertex coloring, distinct central-layer code sets are incomparable; each directed incidence selects a color in the source-but-not-target code, disjoint from every following arc choice. The matching-pair extra color cannot appear on a directed two-path twice because distinct matching edges never meet at an original vertex. A monochromatic incidence arc digraph with no directed two-path on three distinct vertices has an underlying bipartite graph: every mixed source/sink vertex is confined to an isolated reciprocated edge. Signature bit colorings prove chi(G)<=2^t. Central binomial estimates yield the sharp asymptotic leading constant. The standalone exact finite checker validates 16,320 incidence assignments and 819,942 directed two-path constraints but is not a substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Primary Bradshaw–Clow–Xu Proposition 2.5 establishes a log_2 q lower bound and the succeeding remark establishes an upper bound with leading coefficient 2. Axenovich et al. work at broader induced-star-forest level without those inspected formulas. Direct and semantic searches identified no full-text covering result. The 2023/2024 Priyamvada–Panda paper explicitly discusses subdivisions but its uninspected text creates a substantial unresolved access risk; no assertion of historical completeness is made.

value.rationale: The relevant 2023 work explicitly bounds the one-subdivision injective chromatic index between log_2 chi and 2ceil(log_2 chi). A universal upper with leading constant 1 closes this factor-two asymptotic gap for every sequence of base graphs with unbounded chromatic number, giving a concrete constructive rate and natural central-layer design. The paired improvement is not a vacuous reparametrization: it colors the one-subdivision of K_12 using five colors versus a ten-vertex five-color capacity for the unpaired middle-layer construction. Exact finite optimum remains unclaimed.
